short: A British strike aircraft capable of vertical/short takeoff and landing, revolutionizing flexible air operations.
full:
Introduced in 1969, the Hawker Siddeley Harrier was the first successful operational military aircraft capable of vertical/short takeoff and landing (V/STOL). By utilizing thrust vectoring through four adjustable nozzles on its Pegasus engine, the Harrier could operate from improvised clearings, camouflaged forest bases, and small aircraft carriers. This capability was designed to ensure air operations could continue even if Cold War nuclear strikes obliterated conventional runways.

The Harrier achieved global fame during the 1982 Falklands War, where Royal Navy Sea Harriers operating from small decks provided crucial air defense against Argentine forces. The design was subsequently developed into the advanced AV-8B Harrier II by the United States and Britain, seeing extensive service in the Gulf War and remaining in operation today.
